base_override.reason: Two defects make the engine's conservative base unusable as printed. (1) Share-basis break: the FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-24) reports diluted shares on the pre-split basis (110,052,000 for FY2025), while the $67.56 price and ttm.json's share count are post-split (3-for-2 stock dividend distributed February 26, 2026; ~103M shares became ~155M) — so the printed median conservative OE/share of $2.7068 compares a pre-split numerator basis to a post-split price, and the engine's market_cap_est of $7,435,113,120 understates the post-split diluted market cap (~$11.0B at the ttm share count). Split-corrected, the conservative median is $1.8045/share. (2) Sector plumbing: for a broker-dealer/bank holding company, OCF is balance-sheet flow, not distributable cash — conservative OE/share swung $2.71 → $2.37 → $8.10 (pre-split) over FY2023-2025 while net income stayed in a $522,536,000-$731,379,000 band, NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE fires for 2024, and ttm.py's TTM conservative OE is $1.0987/share only because H1 2026 OCF was -$266,453,000 in a half when the company grew its loan book by $2.6B in Q2 alone toward ~$4B of guided 2026 balance-sheet growth and posted record common earnings. The maintenance definition (the engine's own second definition, NI-based) is the defensible owner's-earnings proxy for this sector — the same treatment this sweep applied to IBKR and LPLA — and the median-of-3-FY normalization mirrors the engine's own base method applied to that definition. The resulting $4.2064/share is conservative: it is built on GAAP maintenance totals that include the $180.0M Q1 2025 legal provision year, it makes no add-back for that provision, and it sits below the company's non-GAAP FY2025 EPS on the post-split basis ($7.92 pre-split ÷ 1.5 = $5.28). One known upward bias is retained and disclosed, not adjusted: the CSV's net income is total net income (before preferred dividends on the SF-PB/SF-PC/SF-PD preferred shares), so the base overstates earnings available to common holders by the preferred dividend (FY2025 net income $683,779,000 vs net income available to common shareholders $646.5M per the company's FY2025 reporting) — roughly 5%, absorbed by the widened bear-side probabilities and the low confidence grade. description.text: Stifel Financial Corp. is a Delaware corporation and a financial holding company headquartered in St. Louis. We were organized in 1983. Our principal subsidiary is Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated (“Stifel”), a full-service retail and institutional wealth management and investment banking firm. Stifel is the successor to a partnership founded in 1890. Our other subsidiaries include Stifel Independent Advisors, LLC (“SIA”), an independent contractor broker-dealer firm; Keefe, Bruyette & Woods, Inc. (“KBW”), a broker-dealer firm; Stifel Nicolaus Europe Limited (“SNEL”), our European subsidiary; Stifel Nicolaus Canada Inc. (“SNC”), our Canadian subsidiary; Stifel Bank & Trust and Stifel Bank, retail and commercial banks, Stifel Trust Company, N.A. and Stifel Trust Company Delaware, N.A. (collectively, “Stifel Trust”), our trust companies (collectively “Stifel Bancorp”); and 1919 Investment Counsel, LLC, an asset management firm. Unless the context requires otherwise, the terms “the Company,” “our company,” “we,” and “our,” as used herein, refer to Stifel Financial Corp. and its subsidiaries. We have a 135-year operating history and have built a diversified business serving private clients, institutional investors, and investment banking clients located across the country. Our principal activities are:

about.description_short: Stifel Financial Corp. (NYSE: SF) is a financial services holding company headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, that conducts its banking, securities, and financial services business through several wholly owned subsidiaries. Stifel's broker-dealer clients are served in the United States through Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated, including its Eaton Partners and Miller Buckfire business divisions; Keefe, Bruyette & Woods, Inc.; and Stifel Independent Advisors, LLC; in Canada through Stifel Nicolaus Canada Inc.; and in the United Kingdom and Europe through Stifel Nicolaus Europe Limited. The Company's broker-dealer affiliates provide securities brokerage, investment banking, trading, investment advisory, and related financial services to individual investors, professional money managers, businesses, and municipalities. Stifel Bank and Stifel Bank & Trust offer a full range of consumer and commercial lending solutions.

analysis_md:
# SF — Stifel Financial Corp.
Run date: 2026-10-19. Sector: Finance — wealth management / broker-dealer & investment banking. Price $67.56 (Nasdaq quote API, engine). **Finance sector — the OE/capex DCF fits this name poorly by construction (SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH); confidence is low and the tier is soft.**

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.py output (ttm.json), financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed. Earnings-release and press figures are attributed as cited.

## What it is
Diversified financial services holding company (St. Louis; SIC 6211, security brokers/dealers), operating through Stifel Nicolaus, Stifel Bank & Trust, and KBW. Two engines: Global Wealth Management — record net revenues of $3.54B in FY2025 (company annual report), total client assets a record $551.9B at end-2025 (+10%) and $580.1B at Q2 2026 (+12% YoY, company release), fee-based client assets $224.5B at end-2025 (+16%) — and the Institutional Group — FY2025 net revenues $1.91B (+20%), including investment banking (advisory, equity/fixed-income capital raising, public finance). Consolidated FY2025: total revenues $6,347,533,000 (fundamentals.json), company-reported net revenues $5.53B (+11% YoY), net income $683,779,000 (financials_history.csv), net income available to common shareholders $646.5M with diluted EPS of $5.87 on the pre-split basis (company FY2025 reporting). Q2 2026 was a record second quarter: net revenues $1.45B (+13% YoY), net income available to common shareholders $217.2M ($1.34 diluted EPS, post-split), non-GAAP EPS $1.42, annualized ROTCE 23.6%, and $177M of buybacks (2.4M shares at an average $73.20) in the quarter (company release). The FY2025 10-K was filed 2026-02-24 — before the distribution — and its share counts are on the pre-split basis: FY2025 diluted shares 110,052,000 in financials_history.csv. The $67.56 price and ttm.json's share counts are post-split. Every pre-split per-share figure below is labeled as such.

- **Conservative OE (OCF − capex − SBC), engine output:** FY2025 total $890,938,000 (OCF $1,117,029,000 − capex $62,088,000 − SBC $164,003,000) = $8.0956/share pre-split. Per-share path, pre-split: FY2023 $2.7068 → FY2024 $2.3689 → FY2025 $8.0956; 3-yr median **$2.7068 pre-split = $1.8045 on the post-split basis**. The engine's preliminary run compared the pre-split $2.7068 directly to the post-split $67.56 price (weighted IRR 9.88%, IV@15% $37.61) and printed a market cap of $7,435,113,120 (price × 110,052,000 pre-split shares) — both are basis-mixed; on ttm.json's post-split diluted count of 162,556,000 the diluted market cap is ~$11.0B. - **The conservative series is also plumbing, not earnings.** Net income was $522,536,000 (FY2023), $731,379,000 (FY2024), $683,779,000 (FY2025) — a stable band — while OCF went $499,328,000 → $490,437,000 → $1,117,029,000. For a broker-dealer with a bank, operating cash flow carries loan-book growth, trading and client balances, and deposit flows: H1 2026 OCF was −$266,453,000 (ttm.json) in a half when the loan book grew $2.6B in Q2 alone toward ~$4B of guided full-year balance-sheet growth and the company posted record common earnings (company release). FY2025's OCF spike is an inflow year, not an earnings breakout — net income actually fell 6.5% that year.
- **Maintenance OE (engine's second definition, NI-based):** FY2023 $531,093,000, FY2024 $731,379,000, FY2025 $683,779,000 (financials_history.csv oe_maintenance column; it equals net income in FY2024/FY2025 as printed).
- **Base used — declared `base_override` under bounded authority (c), construction exclusively from this run's printed outputs:** median of the last 3 FY maintenance OE totals — $531,093,000 / $731,379,000 / $683,779,000, median $683,779,000 (the FY2025 figure) — divided by ttm.json's current-YTD diluted share count of 162,556,000 (the only post-split diluted count the run prints) = **$4.2064/share**. ## MOAT — score 5/10 (moderate/narrow)
CAP = clamp(2 + 1.3 × 5) = **8.5 years** (growth holds 2 years, then converges to the 2.5% terminal rate over the CAP; 15-year projection).
- **Evidence first (WORKER_SPEC step 5):** fundamentals.json's `roic_proxy` series is 15.6% (2022), 17.1% (2023) and 20.0% (2024); FY2025 is not computable in that pull (operating income is untagged for FY2025 in both fundamentals.json and the CSV). Gross margin is null throughout fundamentals.json — a financial filer files no gross-profit tag, so the margin leg of the moat evidence is not applicable and the return series carries the argument. Company-reported returns: non-GAAP ROTCE ~25% in FY2025 and 23.6% in Q2 2026; GAAP return on year-end equity (net income ÷ equity from financials_history.csv: $5,294,431,000 / $5,686,770,000 / $5,977,317,000) ran ~9.9%-12.9% over 2023-2025, with FY2025 depressed by the legal provision. Returns above the cost of capital are real but not wide-moat wide, and they are earned in a people business — hence 5, not 7+.
- **FOR:** (1) Advisor-centric wealth franchise at scale — record total client assets $580.1B at Q2 2026 (+12% YoY), fee-based client assets $224.5B at end-2025 (+16%); asset-based fees recur through the cycle. (2) Recruiting engine and culture — #1 in J.D. Power employee advisor satisfaction four straight years (company release); 181 advisors added in 2025 including experienced hires from B. Riley. (3) Diversified second engine — Institutional Group net revenue $1.91B in FY2025 (+20%), investment banking revenue +42% YoY in Q2 2026; wealth and capital markets dampen any single cycle. (4) Through-cycle profitability and capital return — OE positive 5 of the last 5 FY on both definitions; buybacks continuing post-split (2.4M shares in Q2 2026) and the dividend raised 11% for 2026 (post-split $0.34/quarter).
- **AGAINST:** (1) The advisors can walk — client relationships are portable, and recruiting is an arms race (forgivable loans, transition packages) against Morgan Stanley, Schwab, Fidelity and large RIAs. (2) Exogenous gears — asset-based fees ride equity-market levels; bank/sweep net interest income rides policy rates and deposit mix. (3) Investment banking and transactional revenue are deal-cycle cyclical; the Institutional Group has no recurring floor comparable to wealth fees. (4) Supervision/legal overhang — the Roberts structured-products cases forced a $180.0M provision in Q1 2025 (−$1.16/share pre-split EPS impact, company) and related claims remain open; that is a franchise-controls risk, not just a cost line.

## FLAGS — every fragility flag resolved
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH (controlling flag):** Finance sector. Resolved the sweep's established way for broker-dealers (IBKR/LPLA precedent): the OCF-based conservative definition was rejected as balance-sheet plumbing and the base was rebuilt on the engine's maintenance (net-income-based) definition via a declared, fully-sourced `base_override`. Confidence is **low**; a dividend/ROE model would be the right bespoke tool. The verdict's direction is robust across definitions (method range below).
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE (latest FY OE/share 8.10 vs 3-yr median 2.71, both pre-split):** Both are distorted, in opposite directions, by OCF rather than earnings. The latest year is distorted *up*: FY2025 OCF of $1,117,029,000 against $499,328,000/$490,437,000 in the two prior years is a balance-sheet inflow year, while FY2025 net income fell to $683,779,000 from $731,379,000. The median is distorted *down* by the two outflow years. Neither is earnings power; the maintenance-median base ($4.2064 post-split) sits between the split-corrected conservative median ($1.8045) and the latest-year conservative figure on the post-split basis ($5.3971) for exactly this reason.
- **STALE_FY (FY ended 9.59 months ago):** ttm.py was run and its full legs are quoted above. Its TTM conservative OE ($1.0987/share) was not used as the pin: the TTM OCF leg is the same plumbing (H1 2026 OCF −$266,453,000 during guided balance-sheet growth), and fundamentals.json's TTM net income of $953,628,000 plus H1 2026 common EPS of $2.83 confirm earnings recovered rather than deteriorated. The median maintenance base stands; the TTM's role was to supply the post-split share count that exposed the basis break.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE (2024):** Not a one-off tax deposit or impairment — it is structural. FY2024 net income was $731,379,000 against OCF of $490,437,000; the gap is broker/bank balance-sheet flow (loan-book growth, trading assets, client/deposit balances running through operating cash flow), the same mechanism that made H1 2026 OCF negative in a record earnings half and FY2025 OCF spike in a down-earnings year. Consequence: the conservative series is unusable as a base in either direction, which is why the base was moved off OCF rather than adjusted.
- **OE_VOLATILE:** The >3× range is in the *conservative* series (pre-split OE/share $12.9196 in 2020 → $2.3689 in 2024 → $8.0956 in 2025), i.e. in the plumbing. Maintenance OE/share on the post-split basis over the last three fiscal years was $3.1208 / $4.3937 / $4.1422 — a much narrower band (its FY2025 figure includes the $180.0M legal provision). Market-geared cyclicality is nevertheless real, so bear-side weight was widened to 45% combined.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND (share count shrinking 2.2%/yr):** Noted — the engine's −2.17% share CAGR is measured inside the consistent pre-split FY series, and buybacks continued post-split (2.4M shares for $177M in Q2 2026, company release; FY2025 repurchases of more than 5.5M shares at an average $67.24 per the company's proxy summary). The credit is already inside the growth adjustment and inside the per-share scenario starts, which were set against per-share prints; no additional credit was taken.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD (super-bull IV 4.28× super-bear IV):** Real and retained — a market-linked, deal-exposed financial genuinely ranges from a 6.72% to a 19.77% IRR across defensible paths. Consequence per the rules: confidence is low and the verdict is sized to the conservative end.
- **BIG_NET_CASH (net cash 3.53× normalized OE on the corrected base; engine net debt −$1,636,346,000):** The engine's net-debt figure is holdco-tag arithmetic — cash of $2,253,789,000 less the LongTermDebt total tag of $617,443,000 (financials_history.csv) — on a balance sheet with assets of $41,270,782,000 and liabilities of $35,293,465,000 (CSV) dominated by deposits, client payables and trading liabilities that do not reduce to corporate net debt. The company reported a Tier 1 leverage ratio of 11.4% at end-2025 and 11.2% at Q2 2026 (company). The cash pile is noted in the verdict: part of the $67.56 price is a balance-sheet claim, not operating earnings power, which is one reason the earnings-based IRR understates total shareholder return potential — but it does not close a 28% gap to IV@15%.
- **TIER_BAND (bear D 8.97% vs bull C 14.77%):** Resolved by sizing to the bear end: the weighted result (11.70%, C) already carries 45% bear-or-worse weight, and the final tier is the weighted tier with no override; the honest statement of the band is that no case at or above the base case's 30% weight clears the 15% hurdle at $67.56.
